purpose: Multi-lens editorial analysis of all 96 research items and all 32 provisional families. No ground truth respondents or psychometrics.
rubric_note: Manual family-level triage and automated text flags are exploratory editorial signals; they must not be interpreted as validated psychometric scores or confirmed semantic relatedness. No arbitrary quantitative validity scale is assigned.
further_design_risks: Within-group three variants are usually close enough that 2-per-family scoring cap would not permit all three; none are approved.
A family name may disguise multiple questions about the same actual decision; the 32 provisional families are not independently validated.
12-bank to 7-run naive random drawing may omit relevant semantic families, even if the eventual bank has exactly six genuine family pairs.
B axis may require separate consultation/decision measures, but do not change the user-approved 16-type scoring without evidence and explicit approval.
C axis resource amount comparisons and D axis learning skills can measure conditions rather than preferences.
